evidence: Section 4 / Table 2 (r=0.1, n=1,000, three seeds): Qwen3.5-9B GSM8K falls 0.845→0.706 (keyboard) and 0.569 (typoswap) while filler leaves 0.840, establishing the corruption-vs-length asymmetry.

Section 5.3 / Table 5 (GSM8K, n=100/cell, paired cluster bootstrap B=2000): clean attention over corrupted content is significantly harmful in three of four models; joint restoration recovers 45-71% of the gap with significantly positive interaction in every model.

Section 5.4 / Table 6 (n=237, model fixed effects, SEs clustered by prompt): numeric-token hit is the only significant flip predictor (OR 12.89, 95% CI [5.06, 32.85]); corrupted fraction and diversion are non-significant.

Section 5.2 / Table 4 (n=500): length-matched padding control (Group C, 62 tokens, acc 0.662) vs keyboard (Group B, 62 tokens, frag 0.080, acc 0.642); the typoswap row (equal fragmentation, higher accuracy 0.682) is explicitly acknowledged as not following and rerouted to the n=4,160 regression (Appendix H).

Section 6.1 / Table 9: deployable tokenizer-level defense detects corruption (F1 0.77-0.81; fragmentation alone 0.70-0.75) but accuracy recovery is positive in 0 of 8 model-task cells; oracle clean-token restoration fully recovers, localizing damage to input representation.

Appendix K: factorial intervention protocol with difflib position map, -log K mass-preservation correction, and five validation checks (identity bit-identical, causality, mass moves 0.121→0.089 vs clean 0.079); 99.3% of positions get a genuine clean counterpart.
Limitations: factorial intervention run only on GSM8K at a single severity (BoolQ gap too narrow); perturbations synthetic; single-turn standard-length tasks; coupling claim rests on one task.
Appendix D: Llama-3.3-70B GSM8K drops 13 points under typoswap; Chinese CMath keyboard drop of 30 points with harmless filler, indicating cross-script, cross-scale generalization with attenuation.

Appendix A / Tables 11-12 (n=100, r=0.1): GPT-5.4 Thinking keyboard degradation -0.147 vs -0.093 Standard; frontier evidence is prediction-level only and single-severity, weakening strength of that claim.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core-scope LLM research: empirical robustness and mechanistic analysis of reasoning in open-weight LLMs (Llama-3.1, Mistral, Qwen3.5, Gemma-2, plus GPT-4o/GPT-5.4) on GSM8K/BoolQ/PIQA/HellaSwag, with direct hits on LLM, Reasoning/CoT, and Interpretability preferences and secondary alignment with AI Safety/robustness and Prompting. Novelty is solid but not maximal: typo-brittleness of neural NLP is established (Belinkov & Bisk; Pruthi et al. cited in §7); the genuinely new elements are the fragmentation-vs-length controls (Table 4), the factorial attention/content intervention showing the two channels are coupled and super-additive (Table 5), and the evidence-irreplaceability account of task resilience (Table 6-7). Rigor is high: length-matched padding controls, per-example logistic regression with clustered SEs (Appendix H), bootstrap CIs and five validation checks for the patching intervention (Appendix K), and self-scrutinizing controls (OCR fragments most yet is harmless, Table 8; the anomalous typoswap cell is acknowledged). Main weaknesses: factorial coupling rests on one task at one severity (admitted in Limitations), several interventions use n=100, the Qwen factorial cell is ill-conditioned, and frontier-model claims (e.g., thinking mode amplifying degradation) rest on n=100 single-severity API runs. Code/data link and detailed appendices support reproducibility.

primary_link.title: Lexical Perturbations Disrupt LLM Reasoning: An Empirical Study of Attention Diversion

top5.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) achieve strong reasoning performance, but their robustness to realistic lexical corruption remains poorly understood. We evaluate four open-weight instruction-tuned models and frontier models across four reasoning benchmarks under keyboard noise, character swaps, and filler insertion. Character-level perturbations substantially degrade accuracy, especially on multi-step reasoning tasks, while filler insertion has little effect. We trace this asymmetry to Attention Di
top5.summary_zh: 這篇論文探討大型語言模型（LLM）在詞彙層面受擾動時的推理穩健性。作者系統性評估四個開源權重指令微調模型（Llama-3.1-8B、Mistral-7B、Qwen3.5-9B、Gemma-2-9B）與 GPT-4o、GPT-5.4 等前沿模型，在 BoolQ、PIQA、HellaSwag、GSM8K 四項基準上施以鍵盤雜訊、相鄰字元對調與填充詞插入三種擾動。結果顯示字元級擾動大幅降低準確率，多步數學推理受創最重，填充詞幾乎無害；連 GPT-5.4 的內建推理模式也放大而非吸收損害。機制分析提出「注意力轉移」：字元破壞使 subword 斷詞碎裂，碎片在推論時吸引不成比例的注意力質量，集中於中後層；等長對照與迴歸分析證實碎裂而非提示長度才是元凶。因子式介入實驗進一步顯示注意力與詞元內容相互耦合：僅修復任一通道無效，乾淨注意力配上受損內容甚至有害，兩者同時修復才能挽回約 45–71% 的差距。這解釋了拼字檢查、self-repair、Chain-of-Thought 等推論期策略為何無法穩定復原效能，且數字詞元是 GSM8K 失敗的主因。tokenizer 層級的防禦雖能可靠偵測碎裂（F1 約 0.77–0.81），卻無法逆轉損害。研究侷限於英文與 QWERTY 輸入、合成擾動、單輪短任務，耦合實驗亦僅涵蓋 GSM8K。此發現顯示穩健性必須在斷詞發生前內建於表示層，例如字元感知的備援表示、動態重新斷詞與訓練期對齊，深具實務啟示。
top5.title: Lexical Perturbations Disrupt LLM Reasoning: An Empirical Study of Attention Diversion
top5.title_zh: 詞彙擾動干擾 LLM 推理：注意力轉移的實證研究

evidence: Abstract: 'The Kan-default rate is zero in all 248 constrained trials' with failures attributed to reasoning-budget exhaustion or constraint errors, never default reversion
Section 7 (Insight 2): 'With zero events in 248 trials, the 95% upper bound on the Kan-default rate is 1.2%' and jump accuracy 41/44 greedy vs 185/204 at temperature 0.7
Section 7 (Setup): four frontier models on nine certified instances; 'Per-cell accuracies thus rest on six or ten samples' and conclusions rest on pooled counts

Section 7 (Exact-search reference): 'Exact search therefore solves the benchmark by construction. The measured quantity is thus not whether the answer can be reached but whether the model overrides its own default in context'

Appendix F (Aggregates): calibration Kan default in 129/132 non-truncated cases; controls 69/72; 22 jump failures split as 15 truncations, 3 empty, 3 rule violations, 1 valid-but-inadmissible; grader agrees with certified membership on all 138,691 enumerated extensions

Section 8 (Limitations): certifiable and diagnostic regimes may not intersect; scaling certification past brute force is 'the open engineering problem'; calibration validity (C0) could fail for other learners
Section 8 (What is bracketed): 'We formalize four steps of the jump and measure only the second'; constraints are given rather than generated and Tier 2 hosts 'the jump proper'

Abstract/Contributions: code, generator, certifier, and evaluation harness released at https://github.com/EEthanShi/kan-jump-test; Appendix C preregistered integrity checklist including solver, matcher, memorization, format, and budget controls
llm_evaluation.rationale: A formal, LLM-centric capability study: it operationalizes the contested 'jump/abduction' debate for large language models into a measurable Kan-default rate, with certified instances, matched controls, and per-model calibration of the unconstrained default (Section 4.5). Core match to LLM and reasoning/evaluation preferences. Novelty is high: category-theoretic Kan extensions are repurposed from a learning characterization into a certified null hypothesis/foil, which prior categorical and abduction benchmarks do not do (Section 2). Rigor is strong: well-posedness proofs, a family theorem avoiding enumeration, gauge-invariant scoring, preregistered integrity checklist, and explicit assumptions A1-A6; however, all empirical conclusions rest on a single instance family (pointed chains) and small per-cell samples (six or ten samples, Section 7 Setup), and the exact-search reference concedes the benchmark is solvable by search by construction, so the measurement targets only default-override, not difficulty (Section 7, 'Exact-search reference'). Evidence for the scoped claim is solid: zero Kan-default events in 248 trials with a 1.2% upper bound, calibration DC=129/132, controls 69/72, grader validated on 138,691 enumerated extensions, and failure decomposition into truncation/empty/rule violations (Section 7 Insights 1-3; Appendix F Aggregates). Generalizability is moderate: Tier-1 only, fixed FinSet codomain, constraints handed rather than generated, and one task family; the authors scope this honestly (Section 8). Reproducibility is good: released generator, certifier, harness, rendered prompts, replayable pipeline, sub-$15 cost, though evaluation depends on transient API model tiers (Appendix F).

primary_link.title: When the Canonical Completion Is Wrong: Formalizing and Measuring the Jump in Large Language Models

top5.summary: Whether large language models (LLMs) can perform the abductive leap from evidence to a new system of axioms, commonly referred to as a jump, has recently attracted considerable debate. A prominent position holds that LLMs are structurally incapable of such jumps, while recent studies challenge both its mechanism and its evidence. top5.summary_zh: 大型語言模型能否像愛因斯坦從牛頓重力躍至廣義相對論那樣，從證據「跳躍」到新的公理體系？近期辯論一面倒地持否定立場，但爭議始終缺乏形式化定義與可測量指標。本文將跳躍拆解為四個步驟：預設補全為何、何時被迫放棄預設（override）、放棄何時正確、連續跳躍如何疊加，並實測第二步。作者以範疇論定義「跳躍實例」：一個有限擴張問題，附機器可驗證的證書，保證正確補全存在、在重新命名下唯一，且異於資料透過左右 Kan extension 求得的典範補全——後者亦即模型在無約束時的預設輸出。文中證明實例適定（well-posed），並以家庭定理無需枚舉即認證無限多個難度可增的實例。實驗以九個認證實例測試四個前沿模型（GPT-5.6 Luna Pro、Claude Sonnet 5、Gemini 3.1 Pro、DeepSeek V4 Pro），衡量 Kan-default rate（模型固守已被約束排除之預設的頻率）：在全部 248 次約束試驗中皆為零，226 次落在認證正確答案，其餘失敗源於推理預算耗盡或約束錯誤，而非回歸預設；隨機命中機率低至 8×10⁻⁷。作者據此主張：在選擇步驟上模型確實會跳躍；若「LLM 不能跳躍」屬實，瓶頸應在生成約束或發明全新框架。限制包括：僅測量第二步、Tier 2（自創 codomain 與約束生成）尚待研究、以及認證難度與診斷難度難以兼得。本研究把哲學爭論轉為可證偽的量化測試，具重要方法論價值。
